outcome: IgG antibody concentrations against RSV pre-F protein
IgG antibody concentrations against influenza A/H1N1
IgG antibody concentrations against influenza A/H3N2
IgG antibody concentrations against influenza B
Exposure rates to RSV and influenza A/B viruses
Hospitalization cases due to acute respiratory infections
cohort: Healthy infants aged between 2 and 3 months were recruited from communities in Jiangsu Province, Eastern China.
finding: The study revealed a dynamic pattern of RSV and influenza antibodies in infants, starting with high maternal levels that decline by 5-7 months, followed by an increase due to exposure by 18-19 months, with maternal antibodies found to be protective.
